executiveSummary: GM1640's 2025 identity, boundary, centre, 36,108 residents, 32 neighbourhoods, 16 BAG places and eight logical road-border links are coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Leudal combines a direct Maas edge at Buggenum and Neer with the Leudal, Tungelroysebeek, Roggelsebeek, Neerpeelbeek and Neerbeek systems, low-lying Buggenummerbroek, rural drainage and wooded Natura 2000 terrain. The canonical river and pluvial presets replace those mechanisms with municipality scalars: river holds 0.641185 m from T+24 through T+72 and ranks population centres ahead of directly exposed Buggenum, while six nonzero individual hazards and compound share the same eight largest neighbourhoods at the top. Current Waterinfo evidence is one Neer observation plus forecasts only through T+24; T+48/T+72 are NoData. The Buggenum dike is under reinforcement and official material describes Maas, groundwater/kwel and rainfall pathways, but construction need is neither current failure nor current safety. The static road model also misses the current heavy-vehicle/bus/agricultural-vehicle restriction on the N280 Kelperbrug; zero bounded NDW records cannot override that authority notice or mean open. Public registers identify 480 water-control points, provider territories, one grid-planning sample, antennas, education locations and two cross-boundary acute hospitals, but not live topology, capacity, backup, acceptance or restoration. Exact hazard, service and T+72 claims must be suppressed or marked synthetic until governed local evidence exists; missing, empty, stale or horizon-limited data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1640 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM1640 as Leudal in Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord, and report 36,108 residents, density 222/km², 27.3% aged 65 or older and 5,136 one-person households. The reference point [5.891707824586114,51.2414992867735] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Thirty-two neighbourhoods in sixteen districts sum to 36,100 residents, eight below the municipal total (-0.022%); published households sum to 16,145 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 9,860. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 36,108 without rewriting observations.

Sixteen active BAG places are contained: Baexem, Buggenum, Ell, Grathem, Haelen, Haler, Heibloem, Heythuysen, Horn, Hunsel, Ittervoort, Kelpen-Oler, Neer, Neeritter, Nunhem and Roggel. BRT adds 65 settlement labels with different feature semantics. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District-heating and public-charging values are missing in all 32 neighbourhoods; home value is missing once and cars per household four times. Publisher null, suppression or non-applicability remains NoData, not zero. Annual residents omit commuters, tourists, pupils, care users and event-time occupants.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Municipal sewer programme and expired high-water action plan
evidenceSources.edition: GRP 2022–2026 and Hoogwaterplan gemeente Leudal 2022–2023 inspected 3 September 2026; the latter is explicitly an expired edition; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The GRP records municipal duties for wastewater, stormwater and groundwater and treats sewer performance as relevant to health, environment and water nuisance. It is planning context, not a live capacity, blockage, saturation or pump-state observation.

The expired high-water plan at https://www.leudal.nl/_flysystem/media/hoogwaterplan-gemeentelijk-leudal-2022-2023.pdf names local monitoring, barriers, roads and stream controls around Buggenum, Neer, Leudal, Haelensebeek and Zelsterbeek. Its thresholds and assignments must not be presented as current instructions until the responsible authority confirms a current edition.

The old plan illustrates that first-72-hour decisions are location-, level- and role-specific: barriers, seepage-related closures, stream/driftwood checks and weir measures cannot be derived from one municipality flood-depth scalar.
The official pages expose no blanket reuse licence. Preserve publisher, document edition, access time, scope and planning/expired evidence class.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Buggenum dike reinforcement and Leudal stream-system projects
evidenceSources.edition: Current authority project pages inspected 3 September 2026; construction programme 2025–2027; page-level blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The Buggenum dike protects the historic core and does not yet meet the legal norm; the authority is raising it approximately 1–2 m and connecting it to high ground during 2025–2027. A reinforcement need or work status is neither evidence of current failure nor an all-clear.

Waterschap Limburg says Buggenummerbroek can fill from the Maas, rising groundwater/kwel and rain. It may intentionally allow filling for counterpressure/dike stability, then begin pumping while Dorpstraat remains passable at the stated project threshold. This requires boundary, defence, groundwater, rain, road and control states.

The current Roggelsebeek–Neerpeelbeek project page at https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/projecten/herinrichting-roggelsebeek-neerpeelbeek/ describes Roggelsebeek through Roggel joining Tungelroysebeek in Leudal and Neerpeelbeek as a tributary near Asbroek; incised straightened reaches are also drought-sensitive. The project is exploration, not completed protection.
Future Maas2050 reaches, project alternatives and historic high-water monitoring are planning/historical evidence and must not be promoted to current operational state or calibrated protection.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Time-scoped Neer water observation/forecast and Ell weather observation
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026 18:03Z and forecasts retrieved 3 September 2026 04:29Z; KNMI observation/warning snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026; Waterinfo CC0, KNMI CC BY 4.0
supports: Waterinfo has one bounded observation at Neer: 1418 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September, fresh at retrieval and publisher-classed normal/not faulty. A point level is not inundation, dike state, stream condition or municipality-wide safety.

The same point has publisher-classed normal/not-faulty forecasts around 1408–1416 cm through T+24. No local T+48 or T+72 value exists; absent horizons remain NoData and must never be held constant, interpolated into certainty or called normal.

The public endpoint is non-mission-critical and exposes no single model-cycle issue time in the consumed record. Preserve observation versus forecast, station, parameter, unit/datum, observation/valid/retrieval time, quality flags, forecast horizon, licence and coverage.

KNMI contributes one Ell observation at 23:30Z on 2 September (17.5°C, 73% RH, 2.68 m/s wind, 4.53 m/s gust and no measured hourly rain) and an explicit Limburg no-warning publication with a 48-hour horizon. Neither is a 72-hour scenario forecast or all-clear.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current N280 Kelperbrug vehicle restriction and canal crossing context
evidenceSources.edition: Restriction effective 9 June 2026; Provincie Limburg updates through 10 August 2026 inspected 3 September; no authoritative rescission found; page-level blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Because corrosion reduced structural capacity, trucks, agricultural vehicles, buses and touringcars are not allowed over the N280 Kelperbrug across Kanaal Wessem-Nederweert. Public transport line buses and emergency services are exempt; direction, vehicle class and role matter.

The province still described the restriction as in force on 10 August, reported approximately 2,600 trucks normally use the bridge each day and documented height barriers/traffic-control measures. The latest-known state needs an explicit freshness/expiry caveat, not an invented end date.

Rijkswaterstaat publishes signed diversions using N275/N279 and N280/N273/A2/A73 depending on direction. A planned diversion is not guaranteed emergency throughput, and shared corridors remain common-mode dependencies.

NWB 1 August 2026 provides static geometry and the N280 physical corridor but not this class-specific operational restriction. The bounded NDW snapshot has zero applicable records; empty partial coverage cannot supersede the authority notice or mean all roads open.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Flood, nature-fire, utility-outage and 72-hour public guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Current public guidance pages inspected 3 September 2026; page versions, fixed update cadence and blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: VRLN says the Maas, Roer and local streams can produce high water, and describes permanent/emergency defences, pumps, water-level-triggered response, shelter and evacuation decisions. This is governance/preparedness context, not a numerical local forecast or confirmed activation.

Its nature-fire guidance identifies dry/warm vegetation, access constraints, smoke and potentially weaker mobile coverage in some forest/border settings as response concerns. It does not provide a Leudal ignition, fuel-moisture observation, perimeter or spread forecast.

For long gas, water or power outages, VRLN says it coordinates with municipality and operators including Enexis and WML; emergency power and water-distribution actions depend on prioritization and deployment. Guidance does not prove assigned resources, available capacity, backup endurance or completion.
VRLN recommends household preparation for the first 72 hours. Preparedness scope is not measured household stock, universal self-reliance or a service-restoration promise.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, provider territories, grid planning, communications and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed public snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, DUO CC BY; NBNL/RDI exact reuse licence not established in consumed metadata
supports: The HWH clip contains 480 realized points: 16 sewer pumps, 13 surface-water pumps and 451 weirs. All 480 capacity fields are null, 464 name Waterschap Limburg and 16 have unknown manager. Contributor-dependent point coverage does not establish topology, operation, reserve, power/telecom dependency or backup.

Named assets reference Leudal/Tungelroysebeek, Neer/Hanssum, Haelen/Ziep, Neerbeek, Leiverspeelke and Uffelsebeek, reinforcing distinct catchments/controls. Names and point status remain context until an authority supplies connectivity, unit, live control and validity.

A point-territory lookup identifies Enexis electricity/gas, WML drinking water and Ziggo telecom with last-update dates in September 2025; drainage is empty. One Enexis planning sample reports BUGG Buggenum service-area queues and projects, but it is planning context, not live load, outage, spare capacity or municipal topology.

RDI returns 123 antenna records and DUO 27 education records. Locations do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, emergency communications, shelter designation, occupancy, staff or supplies; unknown licence/cadence is preserved where publisher metadata does not specify it.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Cross-boundary acute care and Leudal Natura 2000 landscape context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0; current provincial and Staatsbosbeheer nature pages inspected 3 September 2026, blanket page reuse licence not stated
supports: RIVM finds no acute-care hospital inside GM1640. By straight-line municipal-centre distance, Laurentius Ziekenhuis Roermond is approximately 9.28 km away and St Jans Gasthuis Weert 12.51 km; both report 24/7 SEH and acute obstetrics. Annual rooms/visits and straight-line distance are not routing, acceptance, occupancy, staffing, backup or incident capacity.

The province describes the Leudal Natura 2000 area as approximately 315 ha with deeply incised streams, meanders, wet deciduous forest and hydrologic/groundwater dependencies. Staatsbosbeheer identifies forest, moor and stream-valley terrain in Midden-Limburg.

Static habitat and vegetation make local fire/smoke and access analysis relevant but do not provide current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke concentration, suppression-water availability or safe routes.
The deployed RIVM PM2.5 layer and seismic feed have no local observation/event. Those absences remain NoData/out-of-coverage, not clean air, zero smoke, no ground-shaking risk or an all-clear.

Static NWB gives generalized nominal ceilings, while the latest authority evidence restricts Kelperbrug for heavy vehicles, agricultural vehicles and most buses with defined exemptions and diversions.
There is no ProRail station inside and 61 GTFS stop areas are schedule/geometry only. Zero bounded NDW records never means all roads, bridges or transit are open.

No public input supplies current evacuation/shelter decisions, dike/pump/weir state, bridge throughput, acute-care acceptance, utility crews, emergency water, stocks, fuel or confirmed completion.
The Kelperbrug restriction is current transport context and 72-hour preparation is guidance; neither is a complete continuity or resource guarantee.

At T+24 severity spans 0 for earthquake to 0.904603 for compound; bounded arithmetic is not proof of physical validity.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers close, but missing hydraulic, fire, restriction, lifeline and action dimensions do not gate displayed consequences.
notes: Hazard contributions, service-stage deltas and weighted service-loss contributions reconcile, and public planning/context layers remain non-causal.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent and recovering impacts through T+72 are deterministic but unsupported by hydraulics, operators, routes, care state or confirmed actions.
notes: River keeps 0.641185 m through T+72; affected rises from 7,105 to 7,915 and pressure from 0.279666 to 0.295598 while every service except facilities is exactly unchanged and facilities falls 0.764369 to 0.650569. Burden reaches 633,459.06 without hydraulic or operational cause.

Compound severity falls from 0.904603 at T+24 to 0.454038 at T+72 while flood depth stays 0.474816, affected rises to 24,516, pressure rises to 0.621923 and burden reaches 1,520,700.50; service movements lack action/repair evidence.

Coastal produces zero direct flood/affected at T+24 but residual service burden through T+72; pluvial direct affected clears to zero; neither pattern is validated by recession, dewatering, inspection or restoration evidence.

Only confirmed validity-aligned warning, water-control, defence, bridge/route, care, utility, logistics and welfare actions may alter recovery. Seventy-two hours is preparedness scope, not a restoration promise.

findings.summary: Generated identity, settlements, regional membership and 2025 demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM1640, Leudal, Limburg, Limburg-Noord, the contained centre, 16 BAG places and annual population agree; 32 neighbourhoods total only eight fewer residents than the municipal control and reconcile exactly.
findings.action: Retain source edition/retrieval time, full-resolution geometry access, published-versus-allocated values, null semantics and evidence class on refresh.

findings.summary: Null variables, empty local feeds and missing forecast horizons remain Unknown/NoData.
findings.evidence: District heat/charging are null in all 32 rows, all 480 HWH capacity values are null, provider drainage is empty, NDW has no bounded restriction record, Waterinfo has no local T+48/T+72 forecast and local PM2.5/seismic records are absent.
findings.action: Preserve publisher, version, retrieval/issue/valid time, licence or unknown licence, spatial/temporal coverage, evidence class, NoData mask and reason. Never coerce absence to zero, normal, dry, safe, open or available.

findings.summary: The river preset assigns unsupported direct depth without the Maas, defence and groundwater pathways that govern Buggenum and Neer.
findings.evidence: River holds 0.641185 m from T+24 through T+72 and reports 7,105 affected at T+24, but names no Maas hydrograph/datum, Buggenum/Neer reach, inside/outside-dike state, breach/overtopping, Buggenummerbroek groundwater/kwel/rain, connected footprint, arrival or recession.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing river depth, affected counts, percentages and hotspots until an authority-governed scenario binds hydrograph/station/datum, defence reach/state, controls, direct versus seepage/pluvial pathways, footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData. Retain general flood preparedness.

findings.summary: One Neer point and forecasts through T+24 cannot validate or extend the simulated T+72 flood state.
findings.evidence: Waterinfo records 1418 cm NAP at Neer and normal-quality forecast values around 1408–1416 cm through T+24, but has no local T+48/T+72 value and no municipality inundation/defence state.
findings.action: Separate observations, forecasts, official scenarios and synthetic model values. Show station/parameter/unit/datum, quality, issue/valid/retrieval time and horizon; expire missing future horizons to NoData rather than holding/interpolating or treating publisher class 'normal' as safe.

findings.summary: Pluvial output omits Leudal's stream, sewer, soil/groundwater and control mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.460309 m and 5,859 affected without a rainfall hyetograph, AHN depressions, land/soil/groundwater state, municipal sewers, Roggelsebeek/Neerpeelbeek/Tungelroysebeek/Neerbeek catchments, 480 control points or receiving-Maas level.

Carry resolution, CRS, version/licence, valid time, uncertainty and NoData; otherwise suppress exact depth and affected claims.

findings.summary: Unrelated hazards reuse a population-led neighbourhood distribution that under-ranks Buggenum for Maas flooding.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter and cyber plus compound share the same eight largest neighbourhoods in their T+24 top eight. River places Kern Buggenum eleventh with 168 affected although official evidence identifies the direct Buggenum Maas/defence pathway.
findings.action: Remove shared demographic exposure from hotspot claims. Use separate source geometry for Maas/streams/pluvial, paved/tree-canopy heat, wind/ice, named cyber targets and fire/smoke; render local distribution Unknown until supported and regression-test Buggenum/Neer pathways.

findings.summary: Zero direct wildfire impact is a remote default ignition result, not a local risk conclusion.
findings.evidence: Wildfire T+24 reports zero direct fire and zero affected but nonzero smoke, drought and service burden, while official sources identify approximately 315 ha of wooded Leudal Natura 2000 terrain and regional nature-fire/access concerns.
findings.action: Require explicit ignition/perimeter, versioned fuel/land-cover and moisture, wind, spread/smoke, access and suppression-water assumptions. Keep direct and indirect effects separate; absent local ignition/perimeter is Unknown/not simulated, never a broad all-clear.

findings.summary: The static N280 graph contradicts the latest authority restriction on Kelperbrug.
findings.evidence: NWB models N280 with a generic nominal ceiling and the bounded NDW snapshot is empty, but Rijkswaterstaat/Provincie Limburg state that trucks, agricultural vehicles and most buses are prohibited because of structural capacity, with emergency and line-bus exemptions plus signed diversions.
findings.action: Retain NWB geometry/physical corridor but overlay the authority restriction with bridge/segment, direction, vehicle/role scope, start, end/unknown, exemptions, issue/retrieval/freshness, reason and signed alternatives. Never treat an empty NDW feed as open or count repeated corridor links additively.

findings.summary: Exact water, utility, telecom, mobility and supply availability lacks operator topology and event state.
findings.evidence: Public inputs provide 480 capacity-null water points, Enexis/WML/Ziggo point territories, one NBNL planning sample, 123 antenna records and transport geometry, yet the model emits exact river/compound percentages without live connectivity, flow/load, quality, control, backup, crews, stock or restoration.
findings.action: Keep public registers and planning layers context-only and label operational availability aggregate synthetic/Unknown. Accept only authorized time-scoped operator aggregates or documented manual overrides; do not expose sensitive topology or infer capacity/operation from point counts.

findings.summary: Leudal has no registered acute hospital inside and cross-boundary care is not modeled as an operational dependency.

findings.summary: No current auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger governs consequence or recovery claims.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter, earthquake, coastal and cyber presets remain bounded but locally uncalibrated exercises.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Enexis/WML/gas/telecom/wastewater topology, live flow/load/quality/control state, backup endurance, priority users, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Leudal water outcomes require selected Maas hydrograph/datum, Buggenum/Neer defence state, outside/inside-dike geometry, groundwater/kwel, rain, local stream/sewer catchments, controls, arrival and recession; project pages and point observations are not inundation forecasts.
HWH contributor coverage is partial and every clipped capacity is null; point status and name do not establish connectivity, unit, operation, reserve, emergency power or control authority.

The latest Kelperbrug restriction is authority-backed but operational state can change; absence of a published end or newer rescission is not permanent closure and must carry freshness/unknown-end semantics.

Static NWB, GTFS and provider/care records omit event-time road/bridge/transit passability, emergency/freight throughput, hospital acceptance, shelters, assisted evacuation, home care and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and deprived person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, weather, fire, road, care and utility states can change after audit completion; stale, empty, partial or out-of-coverage data must degrade to Unknown.
